messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary group 'v5.1' streaming p99 latency spike detected. p99=5.8s (SLO=1.5s). Affected route: /stream/generate. Rolling window 5m. Auto-page to oncall.
kim (oncall): I'm on it, joining bridge now — gathering traces + dashboard links.
kim (oncall): @raj can you grab the canary routing table? want to see weight and region distribution.
raj (sre): looking. Canary v5.1 weight = 12% global, concentrated in us-west-2. No errors, just high tail on streaming rpc.
raj (sre): Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd123/streaming-latency?orgId=1&from=now-30m&to=now
sara (runtime): saw similar on our telemetry: KV-cache miss rate up ~3x on canary hosts, and mux queue depth sometimes > 100. Could be cold-kv warmups + a slightly different kv sharding in v5.1.
kim (oncall): can we reproduce locally with small load? we need to know if it's model change or config.
sara (runtime): quick check: model changed tokenization path and introduced multiplexer buffer changes (PR #542). That code path increases per-request concurrency. Might be causing contention at the streaming multiplex layer.
kim (oncall): tom, any customer reports yet?
tom (prod): no direct tickets yet, but we have a few internal ops alerts from support about slow streams in us-west. Not at scale but potential customer impact for long-running streaming calls (websocket clients timing out after 30s).
maria (support): flagged 2 customers on dev tier with timeouts, escalated to Sev 3. They see progress messages but final chunks delayed.
raj (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce canary weight from 12% -> 0% (roll back traffic), 2) patch runtime to re-enable old mux config via runtime flag, 3) increase KV warmup concurrency. Fastest is traffic shift.
kim (oncall): agreed. Priority: reduce blast radius first. Please coordinate rollback if possible.
deploy-bot: Deployment rollback requested: rollback canary-svc v5.1 -> v5.0 by @kim. Approving...
raj (sre): initiating traffic shift now: kubectl patch service canary-svc -p '{"spec":{"traffic":{"v5.1":0,"v5.0":100}}}'
raj (sre): CLI output:
```
Patched service/canary-svc
Scaled v5.1 replicas from 6 -> 2 (drain)
Routing: v5.1 weight: 12% -> 0%
```
kim (oncall): monitoring latency after shift. give it 90s for metrics to settle.
sara (runtime): watch mux queue depth and kv-miss. I pushed a temporary runtime toggle to disable the new multiplexer path on canary hosts (hotfix flag).
sara (runtime): hotfix cmd: `redwoodctl config set canary mux_v2_enabled false` (applied).
raj (sre): metrics: p99 fell from 5.8s -> 1.2s within 60s of shift. p95 back under 0.9s. KV miss rate normalizing.
kim (oncall): good. Customer-facing impact reduced. Logging shows a few aborted websocket sessions during the spike window; support to follow up.
tom (prod): Action items: revert v5.1 PR for mux change, add canary-only load test, and expand local perf harness.
maria (support): I'll open follow-ups with customers affected and provide timeline.
sara (runtime): Post-mortem notes to include: mux_v2 logic introduced request-buffering that increases in-flight memory under certain tokenization patterns -> leads to starvation behind async kv warmups. Need new regression tests for streaming stalls.
raj (sre): For now we will keep canary weight at 0% until v5.1 is patched and a shadow run passes for 24h.
kim (oncall): Handoff: I'm paged out in ~40m. @raj you'll own oncall until next rotation. Leave me notes in the incident doc.
raj (sre): taking over. I'll follow up with a brief incident ticket: INC-4523456789.
kim (oncall): TL;DR: Canary v5.1 introduced mux change -> kv warmup mismatch -> increased mux queue -> p99 streaming spikes. Immediate mitigation: traffic shift to v5.0 + runtime flag disabled. Rest: revert/patch + extended canary shadowing.
tom (prod): ETA for patch & redeploy?
sara (runtime): patch in ~2h, internal QA shadow run ~4h, push to canary with 0%->5% ramp after 24h of shadow.
maria (support): Customer comms: initial email with timeline + apology to affected customers.
kim (oncall): thanks team. Adding a note: severity assessed as S3 (partial degradation) and customer impact limited to long-running streaming calls in us-west. Closing this immediate thread; please add updates to INC-4523456789.
incident-bot: Incident INC-4523456789 created and assigned to raj (sre). Reminder scheduled for 2h to check post-deploy metrics. :white_check_mark:
